questions.prompt: How did Luna and Glimmer help the group travel into the Deep Dark?
choices: Luna led because her eyes could see in any dark, and Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
Luna drew a map of every dark path, and Glimmer carried everyone through the forest.
Luna opened a tunnel under the trees, and Glimmer stayed behind to guard the Hollow Oak.
questions.answer: Luna led because her eyes could see in any dark, and Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.
questions.evidenceText:
Luna led — her eyes could see in any dark.
Glimmer breathed a small flame for the path.

questions.prompt: Why does the whole group enter the Deep Dark together?
questions.rationale: Pip promises to take the frightened creature home, and the group agrees to go together; returning the creature home is why the whole group enters the Deep Dark.
questions.evidenceText:
"We'll take you home," said Pip.
"But the Deep Dark—" said Wren.
"We'll go together," said Pip.
Everyone looked at each other.
"Together," said Stone.

supportingEvidence.evidenceText:
A small creature was at the edge of the clearing.
It had very large silver eyes.
It was frightened.

questions.prompt: What lesson does Pip draw from the creature's journey home?
choices: Bravery can mean finding your way back to safety.
Glimmer's flame was what made the creature brave.
The creature proved its bravery by leaving home.
questions.answer: Bravery can mean finding your way back to safety.
questions.rationale: The creature reaches its waiting family, and Pip calls its run home "the bravest kind"; this shows bravery can mean finding your way back to safety.
questions.evidenceText:
"Yes," he said. "It ran home."
"That's the bravest kind."

supportingEvidence.evidenceText:
The creature ran to its family.
The family gathered around it.
